chunks: As for the one who says that the successor has a son and that the Imams are thirteen,
their assertion is invalid, because of our proofs that the Imams (peace be upon them) are twelve.
Therefore, this assertion has to be discarded.
Reminder: Besides, all these sects have perished, thanks to God, and there is not a person who would uphold any of these beliefs, and this itself is the proof of their falsity.

key_terms.الْخَلِيفَةُ: the successor (often referring to Imam al-Hasan al-Askari)

ai.seo_question: What is the proof for the number of Imams being twelve rather than thirteen in Shia theology?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Tusi refutes the Thirteeners (Thawabiyya) by asserting the definitive count of twelve Imams, a number rooted in the Quranic narrative of Jacob's twelve sons. He argues that the eventual disappearance of these sects serves as historical validation of their doctrinal error, reinforcing the Shia conviction in the fixed number of divinely appointed successors.
